_notes: 2026-07-30: Outbound caller ID was being decided by ALPHABETICAL SORT ORDER. Started as 'what caller ID does Carol Hill have set?' — answer: nothing, so she fell through resolve_caller_id()'s chain to a last-resort phone_numbers[0], and get_phone_numbers() is ORDER BY friendly_name over bare digits, so 61244094006 sorts first: Carol (ext 6966) had been presenting the BATEMANS BAY number while working in WAGGA. Nobody chose it; it would have changed silently on any number add/remove/rename. FOUR independent copies of the priority chain each had their own [0] guess (services/caller_id.py:79, web/routes.py:939, api/routes.py:4913 = the LIVE outbound path, api/routes.py:5517 = queue answer). All four removed; priority 4 is now the explicit tenant default ONLY and resolve_caller_id returns caller_id=None when nothing resolves (documented in module + function docstrings — callers MUST refuse, never substitute). Derek's constraint on hard-failing: 'we need to ensure the user knows what went wrong so they can fix it' — a silent hard fail just trades a wrong number for a dead phone. So the reason is surfaced on EVERY surface: desk phone/mobile SIP get a spoken TwiML <Say> + <Hangup/> (no screen, and /api/voice/outbound serves browser + mobile SIP + desk phones alike per gotcha 12); browser softphone pre-flights the hidden #callerId in makeCall() and shows a PERSISTENT banner (showOutboundOutcome extended with detailOverride + persist) rather than dialling into an audio-only error heard once; /admin/caller-id-overview gets a red banner + highlighted rows + 'None — calls blocked' so it's fixable BEFORE someone dials; logger.error names the user and the exact setting, plus an outbound_call_refused activity entry. TWO BUGS FOUND: (1) the live outbound path (api/routes.py:4909) checked only staff_extensions.default_caller_id then jumped to numbers[0], SKIPPING priorities 2 and 3 — so can_make assignments and section matches never applied to real calls and the admin page's Source column could disagree with what the customer's phone actually showed; now routed through the shared resolver. (2) A latency regression introduced then fixed in-session: routing the call path through the resolver put priority 3's get_staff_directory() on every unresolved call, so it now short-circuits when no phone number has a section (match impossible in that state). I first called that an HTTP round-trip; the boot log shows watson's provider is 'local' (local DB read), so severity was overstated — the guard is still right since the provider is pluggable. DISPLAY FIX so the change is verifiable by the person affected: Twilio seeds phone_numbers.friendly_name with the number's own digits, so Carol would have read 'Calling as 61269316440'; both resolve_caller_id's display builder and web/routes.py::_number_display now treat a name whose digits equal the number as NO name and fall through to the verified_caller_ids label — she now reads 'Calling as Wagga Wagga'. DATA CHANGES applied straight to production (nothing caches these — resolver reads DB per call, tenant records read fresh per request, no cache in master.py or tenant/middleware.py, so no restart needed), each guarded on the target being an active tenant-owned number per gotcha 3: Carol Hill -> +61269316440 (Wagga Wagga); Jihaad Jones ext 6899 -> +61262804443 (Canberra, the only other person on the accidental fallback); watson twilio_default_caller_id -> +61262804443 (was EMPTY, which is why the guess was reached at all). All 21 active users now resolve at priority 1 or 2, so the new hard-fail path is unreachable in normal operation. Shipped as PR #10 (efcaa56, merged 6a258af), deploy run 30520753818 green, /var/www/rinq at 6a258af, gunicorn restarted 06:48:51 UTC, 3 workers clean, no tracebacks. LIVE-VERIFIED against deployed code in real tenant context: carol.hill -> +61269316440 | manual | Wagga Wagga; jihaad.jones -> +61262804443 | manual | Canberra. Also 7/7 on a throwaway harness against watson's real number data (key case: nothing configured -> None, NOT +61244094006). pyflakes F821 clean so the 2026-07-06 CI gate passes; both changed Jinja templates parse. REJECTED — reviving section-based caller ID (priority 3): dead on BOTH sides so a data backfill can't fix it (phone_numbers.section blank on all 8 numbers AND LocalStaffDirectory._ext_to_staff() at integrations/local/staff.py:18 returns no 'section' key at all, get_sections() returns [], so staff_data.get('section') is always None and the branch can never fire). Payoff zero even if both were fixed: only 5 of 21 active staff have a section in address_book (Carol and Jihaad, the two who needed it, have no row); of 13 distinct section values only 3 are offices (Shoalhaven, Batemans Bay, Wagga Wagga) and the rest are departmental (Senior Management, Commercial, Production, Purchasing, Wholesale, Designer Drapes, Customer Success); all 5 who do have a section are in non-geographic ones and already present Canberra correctly. The onboarding gap it was meant to close is already covered by the new admin flag + Canberra default. If auto-defaulting new starters is still wanted use staff_extensions.reports_to instead — that column IS populated and already drives recordings/reports visibility. 2026-07-20: Queue-answer caller-identity fix MERGED + DEPLOYED + LIVE-VERIFIED. Triggered by Shristi Dangol reporting the softphone showing the wrong customer's details during a queue call ('client info overlapping again') — screenshot had the Customer pane naming one person while the 'In this call' panel named the actual connected caller. Fix already existed on branch fix/queue-answer-caller-identity (commit 3d195dc, written + adversarially reviewed 2026-07-13, never merged because merging auto-deploys). Opened PR #1, squash-merged as 3f16ef4, Actions green (lint + deploy), verified live (/var/www/rinq at 3f16ef4, _resolvedFrom present in phone.html, rinq service active). The fix: answerQueueCall() in phone.html accepted whichever leg was ringing but stamped all UI state (context pane, on-call label, currentQueueCallerSid) from whichever queue row the agent clicked; it does NOT change which leg is accepted, only what it's labelled with, plus a guarded server reconcile in the call-state poll. VERIFIED END-TO-END on live watson tenant from SERVER LOGS: queue-answer-click-mismatch fired (clicked=CAb67c8dcce9f77517e3df4fecbaed8e03, ringing=CA9f42fda80d3da8f37ed3d098b0606844); hold verified (three 'Hold request: call_sid=CA9f42fd... action=hold/unhold/hold' against the CORRECTED SID); blind transfer verified ('Blind transfer completed: CA9f42fd... -> 1101', corrected SID); the clicked-but-not-answered caller CAb67c8d was never touched (stayed queued, hung up at 94s); regression paths clean (normal pending-ring answer path 'incoming' and no-ring 'queue-fallback' both unchanged); queue-customer-sid-corrected NEVER fired, i.e. the client-side fix labelled correctly at answer time and the server reconcile never had to intervene; gotcha-32 guard observed working ('voice_call_ended suppressed ... warm transfer still consulting'). REPRO RECIPE for the live system: Test Queue id 8 (only derek active) via +61756258180 (Test call flow -> queue 8); temporarily raise 'send to voicemail after N music plays' from 1 to ~10 or callers get dumped after ~1min; (1) SIM 1 calls and you LET THE BROWSER RING FULLY TIME OUT (~30s) so the caller stays parked (voicemail_on_no_answer=0), (2) SIM 2 on a DIFFERENT number calls and the browser rings for SIM 2, (3) click SIM 1's row. The ring-out gap in step 1 is essential; the two callers must have different numbers (the fix deliberately falls back to the clicked row when numbers are identical/ambiguous); a dual-SIM mobile works as both callers. NEW BUG FOUND (issue #2): 'busy' treated as human rejection — api/routes.py agent ring-status handler ~line 2456 does `rejected = call_status == 'busy'`, but Twilio returns busy for a Client leg ALREADY RINGING for another call, which is not a human pressing decline; the rejection branch then ejects the caller to voicemail if no other agent leg remains ringing. Observed live: second caller entering Test Queue while the only active agent's browser was mid-ring was ejected to voicemail after 3 SECONDS ('Agent derek rejected and no agents remain', queue leave result=redirected time=3s). Masked in queues with several active members (Canberra 6) but LIVE for thin queues: Batemans Bay 1 active member (chris.savage), Wagga 2, Shoalhaven 2. No config escape — reject_action='voicemail' ejects immediately and 'continue' still ejects once no legs remain. UX FOLLOW-UP (issue #3): while a ring is pending the queue list still shows Answer on non-ringing rows and clicking one connects you to the ringing caller regardless; post-fix the UI is honest about it but still confusing. Proposal: while a ring is pending only the ringing caller's row shows Answer; when no ring pending all rows keep their button (that path genuinely answers the clicked caller via AnswerCallSid). LOAD-BEARING SAFETY RULE: whenever the ringing row cannot be identified (withheld caller ID, two waiting callers sharing a number, ring for a caller not in the list) it MUST fall back to showing ALL Answer buttons — locking an agent out of answering is far worse than the confusion being fixed. Minor, not chased: 'Could not resolve tenant for webhook: /api/voice/hold-music' warns on every hold (hold works, falls back to something sane, but hold music may not be tenant-specific — only matters once a second tenant is live). Confirmed queue_continuous_ring and auto_reconnect_enabled are NOT set in the watson bot_settings table (both still off / pending test). 2026-07-08: Per-queue 'voicemail if no one answers' flag (queues.voicemail_on_no_answer, migration 078, commit b0d4fab, deployed — gunicorn restart 00:15:07 UTC, /health 200, migration applied to watson DB). Desk-phone teams that don't watch the browser dashboard (Chris in Batemans Bay + Wagga) were leaving callers holding an unwatched ringing desk until max_wait_time (~5min) dumped them to VM. Now, when the auto-rung team rings out (no-answer/failed) and no leg remains, queue_agent_ring_status (routes.py ~2415, previously only acted on 'busy' reject) bounces the caller straight to voicemail via _send_queue_caller_to_voicemail (no-ops unless still 'waiting', so answered calls can't be wrongly bounced). Flag off = unchanged hold behaviour, so Canberra/The Hub (12 browser agents, dashboard pickup) is unaffected. Enabled on Batemans Bay (2), Wagga (4), Shoalhaven (5); OFF on Canberra (3) + Test (8). Admin checkbox on queue create/edit forms (wired via _update_row present-keys-only). LIVE RING-OUT TEST NOT YET RUN (the exact gap behind the 2026-07-06 incident) — call Batemans Bay, let it ring out, confirm VM; log line 'rang out and no agents remain (voicemail-on-no-answer)'. Also this session: confirmed watson's queue call flows were ALREADY on plain voicemail for no-answer (not AI receptionist as the 2026-06-29 note implied); the only ai_receptionist value was a DEAD open_no_answer_action on the Extension Directory flow id 5 (never reached — that flow's real fallback is extension_no_answer_action, already voicemail) — normalised flow 5 to voicemail so no ai_receptionist string remains. 2026-07-06: Production incident from Friday's deploy — the Phase 2b sweep (5922337) mangled queue_agent_answer: 'def cancel_others' merged into the comment above it (valid syntax, so nothing failed at deploy), leaving the name undefined. Every auto-ring queue answer 500ed; Twilio played 'an application error has occurred' to the answering agent (Hazel/Chris/Shristi Monday morning); customer stayed stuck in queue. Fixed (cb47da1, newline restored) + deployed (gunicorn restart confirmed 23:27:44 UTC). Only instance of the mangling in that commit (scanned all files). Guardrail added: deploy.yml now has a lint job (pipx run ruff check --select F821 rinq/) that deploy needs — verified it flags Friday's exact bug and that the current codebase is clean (1a1f4cc, pipeline green). Post-deploy runsheet smoke test was NOT run on 2026-07-04, which is why this sat until staff complained. Also: reviewed 2 days of signature-validation LOG-mode logs — all real webhooks validate cleanly; only false negative was GET /api/voice/hold-music (no call params -> tenant=None -> no auth token; enforce would have silenced hold audio). Fixed via SIGNATURE_EXEMPT_PATHS for hold-music + ringback (29dd54f, deployed). Enforce flip: wait 1-2 clean business days, then set enforce in .env + restart. 2026-07-04: Full-codebase quality review (7 parallel review agents, ~170 findings) then fixes in 4 phases, all merged + DEPLOYED to production (7bdfb2f..5922337, deploy green, /health 200 on both domains). ba8f1ef Phase 0 live bugs (7: missing import json in admin_schedule_routes, dropped DND check in monkey-patched fetchQueueCallers, callback Call Back never dialled, undeclared consultTargetAnswered, get_twilio_config() in spawned ring thread killed PSTN forwards, blind transfer cancels ringing target on failed redirect, /setup -> admin_required). a30e1cf Phase 1 security/tenant (X-Twilio-Signature validation in LOG mode via RINQ_TWILIO_SIGNATURE_MODE — flip to enforce after watching logs; middleware membership check on domain adoption; get_current_user denies without tenant_users row; tenant-leak singletons removed; setup-tenant uses full provision_tenant(); phone.html name escaping; per-tenant voicemail_requester_email bot_setting). fd39ab0 Phase 2a (db._update_row() present-keys-only replaced 7 clobber-prone updaters — the June ring_timeout bug class; also live: queue saves reset welcome_audio_id/callback_reminder_audio_id/position_announcement/announcement_interval, Peter sync reset hide_mobile; twilio_list(raise_on_error=True) at transfer decision points). 5922337 Phase 2b/3 (capture_for_thread() NEVER worked — threading.local doesn't cross threads; every bg thread silently used master account, masked because watson IS master; new start_twilio_thread() re-binds tenant in-thread, 13 spawn sites converted, fallback logs warning; ~60 silent exception handlers now log via web/util.py flash_error(); _is_queue_paused datetime fix; identity encode/decode dedup). Watch items: flip signature mode to enforce; restore queue audio + hide_mobile values already lost to past clobbers; watch for master-credential fallback warnings; smoke-test transfers + queue ring. Deliberately unchanged: 'tina' ticket tags/permission keys, tenant-DB FK enforcement, call_state.py transient-error misclassification (TODO'd).
